 Live updates from Friday's MotoGP practice at Sepang © Gold and Goose LIVE Sepang MotoGP LIVE: Friday practice updates as Jorge Martin returns
 Live Friday practice updates for the 2026 Malaysian MotoGP at Sepang.
 Live coverage of FP1 and Practice from the 2026 Malaysian MotoGP at Sepang. 
 Key Moments:  
 Red flags due to broken Lecuona bodywork.
 Raul Fernandez pulls out of Malaysian MotoGP.
 Jorge Martin rides with a broken wrist in FP1.
 Friday’s MotoGP schedule:  
 10:45am (local) / 2:45am (UK) - MotoGP FP1 
 3:00pm (local )/ 7:00am (UK) - MotoGP Practice 
 Marc Marquez arrives at Sepang holding the world championship lead by ten points over injured rival Jorge Martin .
 Martin lost the world championship lead and suffered a fracture to his wrist when he fell while battling Marquez for victory in last Saturday’s Phillip Island.
 That ruled Martin out of Sunday’s grand prix, but he was saved from any further loss of points when the race was cancelled due to a lack of visibility for the medical helicopter.
 Martin has been passed fit to return in today's FP1, but - like Raul Fernandez - will be reviewed after the session.
 Aprilia team-mate Marco Bezzecchi will start the Sepang event 50 points from the top, but the RS-GPs could face a tough challenge against the Ducatis this weekend.
 Pecco Bagnaia (Sprint) and Alex Marquez (Grand Prix) won at Sepang last year, when the top Aprilia in the grand prix was Ai Ogura in tenth. 
 Bezzecchi was then the lone Aprilia in an all-Ducati top six on the final day of this year’s pre-season test, with Alex Marquez again fastest and Marc in fourth behind Fabio di Giannantonio.
 Marc had been riding for the first time since his Mandalika shoulder injuries, while Martin - injured at Sepang in early 2025 - was absent due to winter collarbone surgery.
 Peter McLaren 30 Oct 2026 03:26 Trackhouse statement "Raul Fernandez, having started Free Practice 1, in Sepang, has found that the injury to his right index finger (fractured in the course of his Turn 1 crash in the Indonesia Sprint race) is preventing him from riding properly. Following an immediate medical assessment with the Championship Medical Director he has been declared unfit to take any further part in the Grand Prix of Malaysia."

 03:11 Martin improves Jorge Martin pits after his second run, having improved to 19th place, 2.3s from Marc Marquez.
 03:10 Hard rear Some riders - including the KTMs, last year's race winners Alex Marquez and Pecco Bagnaia -  are now trying the hard rear tyre (the medium from last year).
 03:07 Official: Raul Fernandez out MotoGP pit lane reporter Jack Appleyard confirms that Raul Fernandez is out of the Malaysian Grand Prix after just five laps of FP1.
 03:05 Martin returns Jorge Martin heads out for his second run.
 He's now 22nd and last, still 3.9s behind Marc Marquez.
 Aprilia team-mate Marco Bezzecchi in second and KTM's Pedro Acosta third.
 However, don't forget the 'best' tyre compound (the soft rear) is not being used at the moment.
 03:03 "Not easy" for Jorge Martin Aprilia team manager Paolo Bonora tells MotoGP pit lane reporter Jack Appleyard it's "not easy" for Jorge Martin, but that he's "managing in a good way".
 "The key now is how the wrist feels after more laps," Bonora adds.
 03:00 Raul Fernandez out? Aprilia's other injured rider Raul Fernandez was seen running wide at turn one as he struggles to brake with his fractured finger.
 Fernandez then walks out of the pits.
 That could be it for the Trackhouse rider.

 02:57 Tyres Everybody - except Raul Fernandez - is saving the favoured soft rear tyre for now, with most on the new medium.
 02:56 Martin debrief Jorge Martin is debriefing to his team with the microphone. It looks like business as usual for now, and he's set to continue the session.
 02:54 Martin 21st Jorge Martin is currently 21st, 3.9s off the pace when he pits after 3 laps.
 02:52 Marc Marquez in the '58s World championship leader Marc Marquez takes over at the top with the first 1m 58s lap.
 02:51 Bezzecchi sets the early pace Jorge Martin's team-mate Marco Bezzecchi is currently leading the timesheets.
 02:49 Lap records Official Sepang MotoGP Records: 
 Best lap: Francesco Bagnaia, Ducati, 1m 56.337s (2024) 
 Fastest race lap: Alex Marquez, Ducati, 1m 58.873s (2025) 
 02:49 Out lap FP1 is officially underway, and Martin heads out for his first Sepang lap since fracturing the scaphoid bone in his left wrist at the 2025 pre-season test.
 02:46 Gloves on Jorge Martin can't put his own gloves on due to the injury, but once ready, he walks to the end of the garage, stretches, and climbs on his RS-GP.
 02:42 Martin replay Jorge Martin looks up at the TV screen and winces as he sees a replay of his Phillip Island Sprint accident.
 02:40 Jorge Martin A big crowd of photographers is gathered outside the Aprilia garage as Jorge Martin prepares for FP1.
 02:35 MotoGP next Moto2 ends with 2027 Pramac Yamaha MotoGP rider Izan Guevara fastest.
 MotoGP FP1 next.
 02:34 Sepang There's a big difference in past success for Ducati and Aprilia at Sepang.
 Ducati has won nine Malaysian MotoGPs, including the last four in a row and all three Sepang sprints.
 Aprilia's best Malaysian MotoGP result is seventh place.
 Last year's grand prix winner Alex Marquez also led this year's pre-season test, although Marco Bezzecchi set the second fastest lap time on the final day.
 Martin missed the February test due to recent surgery and hasn't been on track at Sepang since being injured at the 2025 pre-season test.
 02:31 Championship standings Four rounds and a maximum of 148 points are still up for grabs, meaning seven riders remain in mathematical contention.
 However, Marc Marquez and Jorge Martin have a clear gap over Marco Bezzecchi, who is in turn comfortably ahead of the group currently fighting for fourth.
